# Examples

Each example is one short script that shows one part of Optora. It runs
on a plain `pip install optora`, prints the numbers it computes and checks
them against a closed form or an independent computation, so a script that
runs to the end has verified its own output. CI runs every script on
Linux, macOS and Windows.

The scripts live under
[`examples/`](https://github.com/navidsharifi/optora/tree/main/examples)
in the repository, one folder per group. For longer experiments that
combine several components and discuss the results, see the
[Tutorials](../tutorials/index.md).

```bash
python examples/01_divergences/01_phi_divergences.py
```

## Divergences

| Example | What it shows |
| --- | --- |
| [Phi-divergences](divergences/phi_divergences.md) | Evaluate the KL, chi-square and total-variation divergences, define a new one (the squared Hellinger distance) from its convex generator with `PhiDivergence`, and compare a whole batch of candidates in one call. |
| [Sinkhorn divergence](divergences/sinkhorn_divergence.md) | Build a ground cost on a one-dimensional grid, evaluate the debiased `SinkhornDivergence` for decreasing entropic strength, and watch it approach the exact type-1 Wasserstein distance, which on the real line is the area between the two cumulative distribution functions. |
| [Maximum mean discrepancy](divergences/maximum_mean_discrepancy.md) | Build a Gaussian-kernel Gram matrix on a finite support, evaluate `MMDDivergence`, and check it against the closed form $\sqrt{(p - q)^\top K (p - q)}$. Unlike a phi-divergence, the MMD stays finite between distributions with disjoint supports. |

## Ambiguity sets

| Example | What it shows |
| --- | --- |
| [KL ball](ambiguity_sets/kl_ball.md) | Evaluate `KLAmbiguitySet.worst_case_expectation` for a sweep of radii in one batched call, check its two closed-form limits, and read the worst-case distribution off the gradient with respect to the loss. |
| [Chi-square, total-variation and CVaR balls](ambiguity_sets/phi_divergence_balls.md) | Solve the worst case over three phi-divergence balls on the same loss, check each one against its closed form, and rebuild the KL ball from a general generator with `PhiAmbiguitySet`. |
| [Wasserstein and Sinkhorn balls](ambiguity_sets/wasserstein_and_sinkhorn_balls.md) | Solve the worst case over a type-1 `WassersteinAmbiguitySet`, where the adversary moves mass along a ground cost instead of reweighting it, and check the closed form for a Lipschitz loss. Then solve the entropic relaxation `SinkhornAmbiguitySet` and watch it approach the exact value as the entropic strength shrinks. |
| [MMD ball](ambiguity_sets/mmd_ball.md) | Solve the worst case over an `MMDAmbiguitySet` built from a Gaussian kernel. A KL ball can only reweight the scenarios the nominal already contains. The MMD ball can also move probability onto a scenario the nominal gives no mass, at a price set by the kernel. |
| [Choosing the radius](ambiguity_sets/radius_calibration.md) | Turn a sample size and a confidence level into a radius with `chi_square_radius`, and check that the worst case over the resulting `ChiSquareAmbiguitySet` is the upper end of the normal confidence interval for the mean. |

## Solvers

| Example | What it shows |
| --- | --- |
| [Gradient descent](solvers/gradient_descent.md) | Wrap an objective and a starting point in a `MinimizationProblem`, solve it with `GradientDescent`, and read the minimizer, the optimal value and the convergence diagnostics from the result. |
| [Saddle point of a Lagrangian](solvers/saddle_point.md) | Project a point onto the half-space $\{x : \sum_i x_i \le 1\}$ by solving the Lagrangian saddle point with `SaddlePointSolver`, using `dual_projection` to keep the multiplier nonnegative, and compare with the closed-form projection. |
| [Robust decision with MinimaxSolver](solvers/minimax_decision.md) | Choose the decision $x$ that minimizes the worst-case squared error over a KL ball of distributions on four outcomes. `MinimaxSolver` runs an outer `GradientDescent` on $x$ and lets the ambiguity set solve the inner maximization exactly at every step. |

## Training

| Example | What it shows |
| --- | --- |
| [Training with torch.optim](training/robust_regression.md) | Fit an `nn.Linear` with Adam on the worst case over a KL ball by passing the per-sample losses to `KLAmbiguitySet.worst_case_expectation`. Radius zero is ordinary least squares. The data mix a large group with a small one that follows a different slope, and a larger radius trades some majority loss for a lower minority loss. |
| [Minibatch estimators](training/minibatch_estimators.md) | The worst case of a minibatch is a biased estimate of the worst case of the full dataset. Measure that bias for the plug-in estimate, remove most of it with `MultilevelMonteCarloEstimator`, and recover the full-batch value from minibatches alone with `StochasticPhiDual`. |
| [Group DRO](training/group_dro.md) | Average the per-sample losses within each group with `group_losses`, and train on the worst group in two ways: exactly on the full batch with `CVaRAmbiguitySet(alpha=0)`, whose worst case is the largest group loss, and on minibatches with the exponentiated-gradient adversary `OnlineGroupDRO`. |

## Adding an example

Put a numbered script into a numbered group folder, for example
`examples/02_ambiguity_sets/06_new_ball.py`. The first line of its module
docstring is the title, and the paragraph after it is the summary shown
above. `python -m tools.docs generate` then writes the page, this overview
and the sidebar entry, and `python -m tools.docs check` fails in CI until
they are regenerated.
